seoTitle: How to Add a Watermark on Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: Learn how to insert a text or image watermark in Google Docs, customize transparency and layout, and apply it across your entire document.
intro: Adding a watermark to a Google Doc — whether it's a company logo or text like 'Draft' — is a simple way to protect a document or make it look more professional. This guide covers inserting the watermark, adjusting its appearance, and applying it consistently across the document.

steps.heading: Add a watermark (image or text)
steps.body: Use Google Docs' watermark tool to insert either a custom text watermark or an uploaded image, such as a logo.

steps.heading: Customize transparency, font, and layout
steps.body: Adjust the watermark's transparency so it doesn't overpower the document's content, and set the font or size if using text.

steps.heading: Apply it across the document
steps.body: Once configured, the watermark automatically repeats across every page of the document without needing to add it manually each time.

steps.heading: Remove or replace a watermark
steps.body: If you need to update or delete the watermark later, return to the same watermark tool to edit or remove it entirely.

steps.heading: Use it for branding or professional reports
steps.body: A subtle logo or 'Confidential' text watermark can add a professional touch to reports, proposals, or shared documents.

faq.question: Can I use my own logo as a watermark in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes, Google Docs lets you upload a custom image, such as a company logo, to use as a watermark.

faq.question: Does the watermark appear on every page automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, once applied, the watermark repeats across all pages of the document without needing to be added manually to each one.

faq.question: Can I adjust how transparent the watermark looks?
faq.answer: Yes, Google Docs allows you to adjust the watermark's transparency and sizing so it blends appropriately with your content.

faq.question: How do I remove a watermark once it's added?
faq.answer: Reopen the watermark settings in Google Docs and choose to remove or replace the existing watermark.
